executiveSummary: GM1655's generated 2025 code, Halderberge name, Noord-Brabant province, Midden- en West-Brabant safety-region assignment, 31,347-person control total, twenty neighbourhoods, five active BAG places, fourteen BRT settlements and five normalized NWB road links are coherent. All ten canonical exercises execute deterministically at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply, and the arithmetic/reconciliation gate passes. Release nevertheless requires correction. Eight nonzero individual hazards and compound reuse the identical full neighbourhood order, while a controlled earthquake at the municipal centre ranks containing Spui 17/20 and a controlled fire inside a 2023-source BRT mixed-forest polygon in Verspreide huizen Bosschenhoofd ranks its containing neighbourhood 7/20. The named-major-river screen produces 1.991441 internal inundation amplitude through T+72, 19,023 modeled people under pressure and 1,153,056 attributable person-hours without selecting a Mark/Dintel/Benedenrivieren boundary, defence or connected footprint; the UI clamps this to 100% inundation stress. The coastal zero is likewise not an all-clear because official evidence describes a sea-river transition system and Mark/Dintel polder drainage. Public evidence supplies distinct high/low polder, Mark-bed, built-up/sandy, water-control, fire, industrial, route and care mechanisms, but none drives the local output. During the audit ProRail reports the Lage Zwaluwe-Roosendaal railway closed from 31 August through 12 September 2026 and four Halderberge crossings closed through 9 September, while the simulator retains only calendar-unbound road proxies. Physical Enexis, Brabant Water, sewer, telecom, care, supply and response topology/state remain unavailable or security-sensitive and were not invented.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: CBS Gebiedsindelingen and Wijken en buurten 2025, BAG woonplaatsen and BRT settlements
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten and Gebiedsindelingen 2025; live services inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The annual CBS/PDOK record identifies GM1655 as Halderberge for 1 January through 31 December 2025. The non-generalized WGS84 MultiPolygon has one component, one ring and 1,955 vertices; the application generalized version has one component, one ring and 101 vertices. Vector vertices have no fixed raster cell resolution. CBS reuse is CC BY 4.0 and BAG/PDOK is Public Domain Mark 1.0; the evidence is official administrative context, not a hazard or operational boundary.

The generated centre [4.5207061357980445, 51.58804666266464] falls inside both geometry products. Five active BAG woonplaatsen—Bosschenhoofd, Hoeven, Oud Gastel, Oudenbosch and Stampersgat—have no generalized-boundary label-point exception. BRT supplies fourteen cartographic settlements across five woonkernen, two deelkernen, two gehuchten and five buurtschappen; BAG and BRT have different purposes and editions and are not population or service inventories.

CBS OData table 86165NED reports 31,347 residents, density 421/km², age 65+ 24.6% and 4,169 one-person households. Published neighbourhood populations total 31,355, eight above the control (+0.026%) because CBS publishes rounded small-area counts; deterministic reconciliation correctly returns 31,347 without fabricating suppressed values.

All 36 expected neighbourhood fields are exposed. Core population, age, housing and accessibility fields cover 20/20; cars per household covers 18/20, while district heating and public charging cover 0/20. Null means not published/not applicable/insufficient, never zero, and the annual administrative dataset is context-only rather than scenario-time exposure.

evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Risicoprofiel and Regionaal Crisisplan 2023–2027
evidenceSources.edition: Official 2023–2027 planning documents; official plan page inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The region-wide qualitative profile has no neighbourhood grid or operational update cadence and states that limited quantitative data motivates expert judgement. No document-specific open reuse licence was found. It is current planning/context evidence, not an incident, probability map, deployment order or T+72 forecast; outside-map and omitted items remain Unknown.

The profile distinguishes coastal, high-river, polder/dike-break and extreme-rain flooding. It explicitly names the Dintel and Mark-Vliet canal, says Benedenrivieren levels depend on sea surge, river discharge and barrier closure, and describes low north-western clay polders where pumps and weirs discharge toward Mark, Dintel and Vliet and extreme waterlogging may persist for days. These mechanisms support local relevance but not the simulator's exact amplitude, defence state or footprint.

Priority regional risks include digital disruption of vital infrastructure, extreme weather and nature fire. The profile separates cloudburst, drought, cold/snow/ice, heat, storm, forest/heath fire, water, electricity, gas, telecom, roads, rail and shipping and emphasizes access/cascade effects. It locates EMS VI earthquake relevance in the eastern part of the safety region, so the remote Groningen exercise does not establish local Halderberge shaking.

Hazardous transport is documented on A17/A58 and the regional railway, alongside road, rail, water, pipeline, stationary-industry and aviation sources. The crisis plan allocates authorities and coordination roles; neither document proves activation, staffing, route availability, resources, completed actions or recovery.

evidenceSources.title: Klimaatadaptatiestrategie 2023, Gemeentelijk Waterprogramma 2024–2027 and local economic/external-safety context
evidenceSources.edition: Climate strategy file 20230222 version 1 using 2018 stress tests; GWP 2024–2027; current pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The 2023 strategy's local climate underlay distinguishes high built-up/sealed areas, high sandy ground, a transition zone, the raised Mark bed, higher old-sea-clay polders and lower polders; it describes the last as very sensitive to water nuisance. The underlying 2018 stress tests and figure are static planning context. No stable machine-readable native raster, fixed refresh cadence, cell size, complete NoData mask or explicit open licence was published on the document page, so the map cannot be reverse-engineered into precise forcing.

The GWP 2024–2027 treats wastewater, stormwater and groundwater separately, states that present/future sewers cannot be sized for every extreme cloudburst, and calls for coordinated public-space, water-chain and private-site measures. It also identifies drought pressure on buildings, infrastructure, vegetation, drinking/process water, agriculture, nature-fire risk and water quality. The plan is policy/programme evidence, not pipe topology, current storage, blockage, pump state or restoration.

The municipality lists about 220 businesses across Bosschendijk, De Gorzen/Oudlandsedijk on the Mark, Industrieweg/Ambachtenstraat by Oudenbosch station, De Hoge Akker, Korenweide, Borchwerf on A17 and Seppe Airparc/Breda International Airport on A58. A current planning assessment separately identifies toxic-transport influence from the Lage Zwaluwe–Roosendaal railway and A17 and the need for warning, sheltering and two-sided upwind response. These are source/sensitivity contexts, not an active industrial release or plume.

The document/page collection has municipal/site scale and irregular policy updates; no standard open reuse licence was stated. Conclusions may validate mechanism and qualitative spatial contrasts, but missing detail remains NoData and every scenario-time state remains Unknown.

evidenceSources.publisher: Waterschap Brabantse Delta / Het Waterschapshuis / WMCN-Rijkswaterstaat
evidenceSources.title: Mark-Dintel-Vliet defences, legal water registers, national water-control objects, Waterinfo and LIWO catalogue
evidenceSources.edition: Regional-defence project completed 9 October 2024; live registers and Waterinfo snapshot 2–3 September 2026; LIWO config 2025.1.6 / project 2025_0_1
supports: Brabantse Delta reports the 2015–2024 regional-defence programme complete on 9 October 2024, including the Mark-Dintel-Vliet section in Halderberge and nearby barrier/pumping works. The water-management programme 2022–2027 assigns the board Mark/Dintel/Vliet navigation, defence, water quantity and wastewater roles. Completion is official context, not live dike performance, closed barriers, guaranteed protection or an event selection.

Brabantse Delta ArcGIS FeatureServers expose legal surface-water, storage, navigation and primary/regional-defence layers in EPSG:28992 with JSON/GeoJSON/PBF queries. Layer-scale geometry and establishment fields are integration-ready register evidence, but server metadata states no fixed update cadence or standard reuse licence. Register features do not prove hydraulic connectivity, compatible capacity, maintenance condition, control or live operation.

The deployment's HWH snapshot intersects 104 objects with GM1655: five sewer pumps, ten surface-water pumps and 89 weirs. HWH IMWA/DAMO OGC data is CC BY-SA 4.0 and provider-supplied with partial completeness; retrieved 3 September 2026. 'Gerealiseerd' is registered asset status, not running/available. Capacity fields lack an app-wide unit/curve contract, and no RWZI or sluice point inside the polygon cannot be converted into absence of those dependencies.

Waterinfo, retrieved 2 September 2026, generally updates LMW points every ten minutes under CC0 unless individually stated. It assigns zero level/discharge points to Halderberge; nearest returned level point is Willemstad-Volkerak about 13.5 km from the centre. Zero in-boundary points is NoData, not a Mark/Dintel surface, threshold, all-clear or defence/control state.

The public LIWO deployment exposes config 2025.1.6 and projects/deltares-rws/liwo/2025_0_1, with working scenario-info and water-depth tiles. It is an irregular expert scenario catalogue, not a forecast. Catalogue release, scenario/model date, native cell resolution, water body/boundary, defence/breach variant, depth bands/units, arrival/recession, licence, coverage and NoData must be retained separately; no selected Halderberge event may be inferred from composites.

evidenceSources.title: Observed weather and earthquakes, BRT land cover, indicative air quality and combustible-nature context
evidenceSources.edition: KNMI observation ending 2 September 2026 23:30 UTC; warning issue 2 September 2026; RIVM observation 2 September 2026 17:00 UTC; BRT feature actuality 2023 registered 2025
supports: KNMI's national station product is ten-minute NetCDF/HDF5 under CC BY 4.0. No fixed station lies in GM1655; nearest Woensdrecht Airport is about 19.91 km away and at 23:30 UTC reported 19.3 °C, 8.39 m/s gust and 0 mm preceding-hour rain. The continually updated CC BY 4.0 warning product reported Noord-Brabant level 0 for its issued 48-hour window. These are observed/issued context only, not municipal fields, scenario forcing or T+72 forecasts; zero applies only to the stated measurement/window.

KNMI's automatically updated FDSN catalogue covers event origins over the preceding 365 days in the deployment bbox under default CC BY 4.0; zero events are assigned to Halderberge. No matching origin is not zero probability or ground motion. An event ID/revision, ShakeMap, site response, building/asset exposure and fragility remain required for local impact.

BRT TOP10NL OGC is national 1:10,000 vector topography under CC BY 4.0 with feature-specific actuality/registration. A mixed-forest polygon 8f087777-ec26-5945-a299-f7bb056ee9cf has source actuality 2023, was registered February 2025 and intersects BU16550509 Verspreide huizen Bosschenhoofd. The IPO combustible-nature WMS is Public Domain context with metadata updated 19 February 2026 and cadence unstated. Land cover/eligibility does not establish ignition, moisture, spread, smoke, access, extinguishing water or suppression; stale and missing polygons remain Unknown.

RIVM's indicative hourly network has no GM1655 station; nearest retrieved PM2.5 point is Zevenbergen-Galgenweg about 8.82 km away at 4.7 µg/m³. The service states no standard reuse licence and data can be revised. A point reading is not a Halderberge exposure surface, source attribution, smoke plume or scenario forecast.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijkswaterstaat / ProRail / OVapi / NDW / Waterschap Brabantse Delta
evidenceSources.title: NWB roads, railway/station, scheduled transit, current rail works, waterways and current road situations
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 1 August 2026; GTFS 9543 valid 30 August–12 December 2026; ProRail notice 26 August 2026 valid 30 August–12 September; NDW publication 2 September 2026 15:25 UTC
supports: Monthly CC0 NWB produces five logical GM1655 edges: A17 to Roosendaal and Moerdijk, A58 to Rucphen, N268 to Steenbergen and N640 to Etten-Leur. The two A17 edges are consecutive parts of one physical corridor and non-additive. Generalized 150/260 scenario-unit capacities are not observed vehicles, emergency access, freight, aid or supply throughput; source=NWB correctly permits only Mobility and explicitly assumed road logistics/Supply.

ProRail's manually maintained CC0 OGC exposes the Lage Zwaluwe–Roosendaal track and Oudenbosch station. OVapi GTFS 9543 provides 34 stop areas as free-use, best-effort scheduled context without operational SLA. Static geometry/schedules do not prove availability, passenger capacity, evacuation, accessibility or recovery.

A ProRail notice dated 26 August 2026 states that no passenger or freight trains operate Lage Zwaluwe–Roosendaal from 31 August through 12 September, and Galgestraat plus Industrieweg-Zeggeweg in Oudenbosch and Noordhoeksestraat plus Sint Maartenstraat in Oud Gastel are closed to every road user from 30 August 23:00 through 9 September 06:00. This is event-valid planned operational context during the audit, but the simulator has no selected reference date/rail edge/crossing adapter and must not project it outside its validity window.

Brabantse Delta manages Mark/Dintel navigation; its legal navigation register and RWS FIS-VNDS are static geometry/attribute sources, not waterway or bridge operating state. Road, rail, overway, waterway and water-level dependencies require distinct dated records and cannot be merged into one inferred access value.

The CC0 NDW DATEX snapshot covers real/no-restriction road records intersecting publication time through 72 hours; zero records were assigned to GM1655. Zero matching records means no covered report, not that A17/A58/N268/N640, local crossings, rail or Mark/Dintel navigation are open.

evidenceSources.publisher: Stichting Mijn Aansluiting / Netbeheer Nederland / RIVM / DUO / RDI / Register Externe Veiligheidsrisico's
evidenceSources.title: Provider territories, grid planning, acute care, education, antenna and industrial-risk registers
evidenceSources.edition: Live provider query 3 September 2026; deployment snapshots 2–3 September 2026; RIVM acute care v1.1 published 3 July 2026
supports: A Public Domain WMS point query at the municipal centre identifies Enexis electricity/gas (record update 7 September 2025), Brabant Water drinking water (29 December 2025) and Ziggo media (7 September 2025), but returns no drainage polygon. These are provider-supplied responsibility territories at one point, not full municipal coverage, cable/pipe/sewer topology, connectivity, quality, outage or restoration. Empty drainage is NoData/Unknown.

Netbeheer Nederland's one-postcode sample at 4731VW identifies Enexis RSD Roosendaal planning-area withdrawal 245.9 MW existing/119 MW required/95.2 MW queued across 178 requests and injection 237/143.4/37.7 MW across 83 requests, with nineteen projects. Capacity/projects update at least quarterly and queues monthly; the publisher calls the product open but exact licence and frontend endpoint stability are unstated. One large-user planning sample is not current load, household capacity, topology, outage, reserve or T+72 restoration.

RIVM acute-care questionnaire v1.1 is national CC0 questionnaire data published 3 July 2026. It has no SEH point inside GM1655; nearest is Bravis Roosendaal about 8.74 km away, reporting 24/7 SEH, thirteen rooms and 13,298 visits in 2025 but no acute obstetrics. Bravis Bergen op Zoom and Amphia Breda add cross-boundary context. Dated offers are not live occupancy, acceptance/diversion, staffing, generator endurance, supplies, route state or recovery.

The snapshot contains twenty DUO education locations (daily refresh about 06:15, CC BY version unspecified) and 69 RDI antenna installations—thirty mobile, twenty fixed link, one broadcast and eighteen amateur—from a statutory WFS with cadence/reuse licence unstated. Schools are not shelters; antennas are not ownership, coverage, backhaul, power/backup, capacity or operational state.

REV public WMS depicts regulated activity and attention areas with feature-scale geometry; service cadence, record-valid time and reuse licence were not stated. It is industrial source context, not an incident, release rate, plume, evacuation/shelter order or control state. Missing features never prove zero risk. Every public layer remains affectsSimulation=false until a reviewed causal adapter is supplied.

evidenceSources.title: National first-72-hour household preparedness guidance
supports: National guidance recommends supplies for 72 hours, including three litres of water per person per day, food, radio, power bank and medicines. Rijksoverheid material is CC0 unless otherwise stated, but this is national public information with household/self-report spatial resolution, no operational cadence and no event-valid municipal measurement.

The 72-hour horizon means residents should prepare for delayed help; it is not measured Halderberge preparedness, a promised aid arrival, a resource inventory or a restoration deadline. Household stocks, reception/distribution capacity, opened facilities, mutual aid, crews, vehicles, fuel, spares, medicines and completed actions remain Unknown without time-stamped authority confirmation.

identity.summary: Official code, name, province, safety region, centre and headline population agree.
notes: Manifest, generated collection and official sources uniquely identify GM1655 as Halderberge in Noord-Brabant and Veiligheidsregio Midden- en West-Brabant.
Boundary and statistics edition 2025, older stress-test inputs, multi-year plans, current observations/notices and synthetic scenario time remain distinct.
No identity, centre-containment, province, safety-region or headline-population contradiction was found.

geography.summary: Full and generalized 2025 geometry retain the complete one-part municipality without detached components.
notes: The full geometry has one component, one ring and 1,955 vertices; the overview geometry has one component, one ring and 101 vertices. All five BAG labels lie within the generalized boundary.

The municipality spans distinct sandy/built-up, Mark-bed and polder regimes documented in E03; administrative containment cannot substitute for catchment, dike ring, flood compartment, fire fuel, plume or service area.
The generated centre lies in BU16550304 Spui and is a label/reference point, not an operational hub or hydraulic centroid.

notes: Official/generated population is 31,347, density 421/km², age65Pct 24.6 and one-person households 4,169.
Neighbourhoods total 31,355, eight above the control (+0.026%); the allocation contract reconciles exactly to 31,347.

Largest published neighbourhoods are Oud Gastel 5,870, Hoeven 4,795, Oudenbosch-Centrum 4,550, Bosschenhoofd 2,235 and Pagnevaart 2,155. Counts do not identify transient demand, medical dependency, visitors or household stocks.

regionalDetail.summary: All twenty neighbourhoods load, but climate, operational-hazard and lifeline coverage is incomplete and non-causal.
notes: All core fields cover 20/20 and cars per household 18/20; district heating and public charging cover 0/20 and remain NoData.
The municipal climate figure, 104 water objects, 69 antennas, twenty education locations, one planning-area sample and external hospital points add context but no complete live operational surface.
Every local layer must retain source, edition/valid time, resolution, coverage, licence, uncertainty, NoData and affectsSimulation.

settlements.summary: Five BAG places and fourteen BRT settlement features are coherent contextual labels.
notes: All five active BAG woonplaatsen match the expected Halderberge cores with no out-of-boundary label-point flag.
BRT's fourteen woonkern/deelkern/gehucht/buurtschap records preserve cartographic classifications without creating residents or services.
Settlement labels do not establish incident occupancy, isolation, utility connection, shelter role or evacuation throughput.

transport.summary: Static road/rail/transit geometry is coherent, but a current ProRail closure and multimodal dependencies are absent from simulation state.

Oudenbosch station and 34 GTFS stops are static context. At audit time no passenger/freight trains run Lage Zwaluwe–Roosendaal, and four Halderberge crossings have dated closures, yet no scenario reference-date/rail/crossing state is bound.

Mark/Dintel navigation, roads, railway, crossings, Bravis access and cross-boundary aid/supply require separate event-valid capacity and passability. Zero NDW records proves no covered report, never open access.

emergencyContext.summary: Roles, context points and 72-hour advice exist, but no event-valid actions, resources, facilities or mutual-aid state is supplied.
notes: VRMWB plans define regional coordination, GHOR/brandweer/police and municipal roles but do not prove activation, staffing, requested resources or completion.
External Bravis/Amphia facilities and schools do not establish acceptance/diversion, opened reception, occupants, staff, water/power backup, fuel, medicines, routes or supply throughput.

notes: The gate covers severe storm, pluvial flood, river flood, coastal flood, heatwave, winter storm, cyberattack, earthquake, wildfire and compound at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 for all eight services.

T+24 severity / affected people-equivalent / cumulative local pre-network event-attributable person-hours are storm 0.031612 / 3,222 / 73,446.26; pluvial 0.238914 / 3,861 / 106,720.88; river 0.628415 / 17,872 / 291,613.82; coastal 0.024657 / 0 / 15,325.99; heat 0.071754 / 0 / 51,788.71.

Remaining T+24 values are winter 0.483589 / 6,889 / 130,866.19; cyber 0.423669 / 8,558 / 161,550.90; earthquake 0 / 0 / 1,845.76 after a tiny earlier signal; wildfire 0.132973 / 0 / 48,210.63; compound 0.812846 / 18,513 / 295,617.99.

Affected population is a modeled people-equivalent and person-hours is matched-baseline weighted service shortfall—not identified customers, casualties, displacement, economic loss or operator telemetry.

numericalInvariants.summary: Determinism, finite bounds, reconciliation, ledger closure, counterfactual and monotonic-burden checks pass.
notes: MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM1655 pnpm audit:model passes both municipality-coverage tests.

All twenty local rows reconcile to 31,347 residents and municipal demand/delivery; no-event attribution is zero, service-layer selection leaves physical hazard invariant and repeated output is deterministic.
Passing arithmetic contracts does not calibrate water, weather, fire, industrial, seismic, cyber, access, utility or recovery behavior.

spatialPlausibility.summary: Eight unrelated nonzero hazards reuse one exact neighbourhood order, and both controlled sources fail containment ranking.
notes: At T+24 storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire—and compound—share the same complete order: Hoeven, Verspreide huizen Stampersgat, Stampersgat, Verspreide huizen Oud Gastel and Achter 't Hof lead; Verspreide huizen ten noorden van Oudenbosch is last. Canonical earthquake is an all-zero tie at that checkpoint.
A controlled earthquake at [4.5207061357980445, 51.58804666266464] lies in Spui but containing Spui ranks 17/20 at T+6 while municipality ground motion is 0.196539 g and severity 0.614186.

A controlled fire at [4.555489777366474, 51.57100374426068] lies in a 2023-source BRT mixed-forest polygon and BU16550509 Verspreide huizen Bosschenhoofd, but the containing neighbourhood ranks 7/20 at T+24 while direct flame is 0.599363, smoke 0.588533 and severity 0.607002.
The fixtures test allocation only and are not incidents. Official high/low polders, Mark bed, built-up/sandy zones and eligible woodland independently refute a universal seed.

serviceDependencies.summary: Inspectable service ledgers are not calibrated to Halderberge water controls, utilities, crossings, care or industrial dependencies.
notes: Source=NWB appropriately limits road edges to Mobility and assumed road logistics/Supply, but generalized capacity does not encode the current rail/overway closure, road passability, Mark/Dintel navigation, emergency priority or observed throughput.

Provider territories, one grid-planning sample, 104 water objects, 69 antennas, schools and external hospitals remain affectsSimulation=false and do not validate topology, compatible capacity, switch/pump state, pressure/quality, backhaul, backup or restoration.
Wastewater, stormwater/polder drainage, drinking water and defence/navigation control are separate chains. Registered objects and completed projects cannot justify exact water/drainage availability.

causalTrace.summary: Generic evidence classes and NoData warnings are visible, but exact Halderberge values lack adjacent family-specific release caveats.
notes: Desktop 1440×1000 and mobile 375×812 checks had no horizontal overflow or browser errors; mobile Details was reachable and aria-live announced the selected municipality/time.

At river T+72 both viewports show Halderberge '100% inundation stress' and 'Scenario · evidence class derived-screening'; desktop aria-live announces 63% scenario severity. The inspector correctly says zero Halderberge Waterinfo points means NoData, displays LIWO as scenario-selection context, and identifies the nearest KNMI station as non-interpolated context.

No adjacent municipality-specific warning names the unselected Mark/Dintel boundary, defence/breach/control state, polder connection, 2018 local climate inputs, current ProRail restriction, source-containment defect or action/resource gap. Generic derived-screening language does not qualify exact affected/service/recovery values.

findings.summary: Eight unrelated individual hazards and compound use exactly the same twenty-neighbourhood order.
findings.evidence: At T+24 storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire all rank Hoeven, Verspreide huizen Stampersgat, Stampersgat, Verspreide huizen Oud Gastel and Achter 't Hof first through fifth and Verspreide huizen ten noorden van Oudenbosch last. E03/E04 distinguish built-up/sandy, Mark-bed, high/low-polder and managed-water mechanisms; E05 supplies separate forest context.
findings.action: Mark all nine current local hazard-family distributions Unsupported/Unknown and prohibit deployment use. Replace the shared hash with family-specific, coverage-aware official surfaces/targets; retain native event, date, CRS/resolution, units/classes, coverage, validation, licence and NoData.

findings.summary: Controlled local earthquake and woodland-fire sources do not prioritize their containing neighbourhoods.
findings.evidence: Centre earthquake ground motion 0.196539 g leaves Spui 17/20. A synthetic source inside 2023-source BRT mixed forest and BU16550509 produces flame 0.599363/smoke 0.588533 but ranks its containing Bosschenhoofd rural neighbourhood 7/20. Both rankings repeat the common seed.
findings.action: Enforce event/source containment and distance before vulnerability allocation. Earthquake must require selected event/ShakeMap/site/fragility; fire must separate ignition/perimeter, eligible fuel, moisture, wind, barriers, access, firewater and suppression. Keep fixtures explicitly synthetic.

findings.summary: A severe persistent named-major-river result lacks a selected Mark/Dintel/Benedenrivieren scenario and defence state.
findings.evidence: River forcing reaches internal flood amplitude 1.991441 by T+12 and holds it through T+72, producing 19,023 affected, 1.153 million person-hours and 18.14% drainage availability. The UI clamps this to 100% inundation stress. E02–E04 confirm real relevance but distinguish storm-surge/river transition, Dintel/Mark-Vliet, polders, controls and defences; none selects the modeled footprint.
findings.action: Retain the number only as a non-operational diagnostic and expose local river impact as Unknown. Require a pinned expert-reviewed LIWO/Brabantse Delta scenario with boundary/hydrograph, datum, defence/breach/control state, connected footprint, probability, arrival/recession, resolution, bands/units, coverage, licence and NoData.

findings.summary: Local polder, rain, sewer and managed-water mechanisms do not drive pluvial or drainage causality.
findings.evidence: The model gives pluvial 0.330804 flood and 52.29% drainage availability at T+24 using the shared spatial seed. E03 distinguishes high sealed/sandy, Mark-bed and high/low-polder regimes; E04 supplies 104 static objects and says zero in-boundary Waterinfo points. No catchment, flow direction, receiving level, live pump/weir, sewer/storage, blockage, power/backup or emptying state is bound.
findings.action: Integrate an authorized native local stress-test successor and Brabantse Delta catchment/control data while keeping wastewater, stormwater/polder drainage, drinking water and defences separate. Static points stay contextual; no observation or provider match remains Unknown rather than zero.

findings.summary: Storm, heat/drought, winter, cyber and remote-earthquake values lack event-valid local forcing or target state.
findings.evidence: Nearest weather observation is 19.91 km away and is not interpolated; the warning zero covers only its issued 48-hour window. The canonical Groningen source leaves only a 0.004341 peak trace and 3,299.12 person-hours by T+72 without an event/ShakeMap/site/fragility chain. Cyber has exact target/service effects without an identified system or incident. E02 says earthquake relevance is the eastern safety-region area, not that Halderberge is hazard-free.
findings.action: Keep these as labelled exercises and mark municipality distribution/impact Unsupported. Bind timestamped forecast/observation grids or explicit event/target fixtures; do not turn catalogue absence, warning zero or remote distance into an all-clear or damage forecast.

findings.summary: The remote-smoke wildfire exercise and absent industrial preset do not cover documented local woodland and hazardous-source pathways.
findings.evidence: Canonical wildfire produces zero local flame but smoke 0.256223 and drought 0.681071 at T+24; the local Bosschenhoofd containment fixture fails. E02/E03 document woodland/firewater concerns, A17/A58/rail hazardous transport, Mark-side/logistics industry, Borchwerf and Seppe Airparc, while REV and BRT remain context-only. residualLimitations: The municipal 2018 climate stress-test figure is useful planning evidence but lacks a published stable native raster/API contract, fixed cell size, refresh cadence, complete NoData mask and explicit open licence; it was not digitized from the PDF.
LIWO 2025.1.6 / 2025_0_1 supplies an expert catalogue, not a selected Mark/Dintel event. Catalogue release and model/scenario date, resolution, variants, bands, coverage and NoData remain distinct.
The ProRail closure is valid only for stated August–September 2026 intervals. It cannot be projected into calendar-unbound exercises or treated as permanent network capacity.

Physical utility, sewer, telecom, facility, hospital, industrial-control and emergency-logistics topology/state may be unavailable or security-sensitive; no public register was promoted to operational truth.
Controlled earthquake and Bosschenhoofd woodland sources are synthetic regression fixtures, not observed events or forecasts.
